# Sundarīnandātherīgāthā (Thig 5.4)

**ID:** Thig 5.4

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sundarīnandātherīgāthā* (Thig 5.4) comprises verses 82–86 within the five-verse section (Pañcakanipāta) of the *Therīgāthā* [Collett 2014]. The verses are attributed to the elder nun Sundarīnandā, identified in traditional sources as the daughter of Mahāprajāpatī and King Śuddhodana, making her the Buddha's half-sister and full sister of Nanda; she was known as Sundarīnandā on account of her great physical beauty [Bodhi 2012; Collett 2014; Encyclopedia of Buddhism 2004].

In his commentary on the *Therīgāthā* (*Paramatthadīpanī*), Dhammapāla explains that in the time of the Buddha Padumuttara in Haṁsavatī, she aspired to become foremost among nuns who practice meditation, an aspiration fulfilled when she took rebirth in the Sakyan royal family in the time of Gotama Buddha [Collett 2014]. Her narrative and verse themes closely parallel and sometimes overlap with biographical traditions surrounding other nuns sharing the name Nandā, such as Abhirūpanandā and Rūpanandā [Collett 2014].
